intro: Dancing Script font is one of the most-used free script typefaces on the web: a casual, lively cursive with a bouncing baseline, drawn by Pablo Impallari and published on Google Fonts under the SIL Open Font License. This page shows you what it looks like, where to get the real font file for free, and gives you a generator for Unicode script text in the same friendly mood — for the bios, captions and display names where a font file cannot go.
copyHeading: Dancing Script Lookalike Text: Copy and Paste
copyBody: Type a name or phrase, compare the previews, and press Copy beside the one you like. What you copy is Unicode script — 𝒮𝓌ℯℯ𝓉 and 𝓢𝔀𝓮𝓮𝓽 — not the Dancing Script font itself, because a text field cannot carry a typeface. The lookalike keeps the casual, rounded, slightly bouncy feel and works in Instagram bios, TikTok names, WhatsApp statuses and anywhere else that has no font picker. For a design, a website or a document, use the real font from the download section below.
popularTitle: What Dancing Script Font Looks Like
popular: Dancing Script is a casual connected script with medium contrast, rounded terminals and letters that bounce a little above and below the baseline, which is where the name comes from. It reads as friendly and informal rather than formal or calligraphic, and it comes in a variable weight from Regular to Bold. The closest Unicode match is regular script (𝒮𝓌ℯℯ𝓉) for the light weight and bold script (𝓢𝔀𝓮𝓮𝓽) for the heavy end; italic (𝑆𝑤𝑒𝑒𝑡) is a calmer alternative when the bounce is too much. A small heart, flower or bow around the word matches the cards and invitations the font usually appears on.

socialTitle: Dancing Script for Canva, Websites and Bios
social: Dancing Script shows up everywhere casual script is wanted: Canva templates, wedding and party invitations, small-business logos, blog headings and Etsy listings. In those places you can use the real font — it is built into Canva and installable in any design or office app. The one place it cannot go is a social profile: Instagram, TikTok and Discord have no font setting, so the Unicode script from the generator above is the practical substitute for a display name or bio line. Keep hashtags and links plain either way.
limitNote: the Unicode lookalike is a fixed set of characters, so it cannot reproduce Dancing Script's bounce, weight axis or letter connections exactly — it matches the mood, not the metrics.
specificTitle: Dancing Script Font vs Pacifico, Great Vibes and Brush Script
specific: Among the free Google script fonts, Dancing Script is the friendly middle: less heavy and retro than Pacifico, less formal and thin than Great Vibes, less rough than a brush script. That is why it is the default choice for invitations, greeting cards and casual logos. If you want the same feel with more weight, the brush script page on this site covers heavier Unicode script; if you want elegance, the elegant cursive signature page leans that way.

uniqueH2: Download Dancing Script Free, and When to Use the Lookalike
uniqueBody: For anything you design, use the genuine font. Open the Google Fonts page, press Download family, and install the TTF on Windows or macOS; it then appears in Word, PowerPoint, Photoshop and every other app's font menu. On a website, embed it with the Google Fonts link tag or self-host the files. Canva already includes it under the name Dancing Script, so nothing needs installing there. The Open Font License allows personal and commercial use, including in logos and products, with no attribution required.

Use the Unicode lookalike from the generator above when there is no font menu at all: an Instagram or TikTok display name, a bio, a Discord nickname, a WhatsApp status, a plain-text email signature. Those fields accept characters, not fonts, so the only way to look scripted is to paste characters that are already drawn in a script style. The result reads as the same casual mood at profile size, even though the letterforms are not Dancing Script's.

The honest gap between the two: the lookalike cannot bounce, cannot connect letters with real ligatures and has one fixed weight per alphabet. If a client or a printed piece is involved, the real font is the right tool every time. If the goal is a friendly script line in a place that only takes text, the generator gets you there in a few seconds.

How do I download and install Dancing Script?
Open its Google Fonts page, press Download family, unzip, and double-click the TTF to install on Windows or macOS. It then appears in the font menu of Word, Canva desktop, Photoshop and other apps.
Yes. Canva includes Dancing Script in its font list for free accounts, so you can select it directly without installing anything.
Can I use Dancing Script in my Instagram bio?
Not the font itself — Instagram has no font setting. Use the generator on this page to copy Unicode script in a similar casual style, and paste that into your bio or name.
Does the generator produce the actual Dancing Script letters?
No. It produces standard Unicode script characters that share the friendly, rounded mood. The real letterforms, bounce and weight axis only exist in the font file.
What weights does Dancing Script come in?
It is a variable font with a weight axis from Regular (400) to Bold (700), so any weight in between can be used in apps that support variable fonts.
Pablo Impallari designed it, with later versions contributed by the open-source community. It has been on Google Fonts since 2011.
